person: A 79-year-old widow in suburban Auckland, New Zealand, who grows orchids and wants patient help managing cloud photo storage.
situation: A community garden has more interested residents than available plots.

instance.task_summary: Draft an English email proposing a fair shared-plot arrangement to a casual gardening acquaintance after an oversubscribed allocation.
givens: The sender knows Mara casually from two working bees at the Kowhai Community Garden.
Fourteen residents applied for eight plots, and the coordinator offered the sender and Mara one shared 3 m × 2 m plot.
The sender wants to propose dividing the bed equally, alternating weekly watering, and discussing purchases before either person spends more than NZ$20.
The sender can water on Wednesday and Sunday mornings but cannot lift compost bags because of arthritis.
The arrangement must remain a proposal rather than an assumption that Mara has agreed.

constraints.text: Use clear, natural English appropriate for an Auckland community-garden email.
Acknowledge that sharing may not suit Mara and invite her to suggest a different arrangement.
Include the proposed division, watering schedule, spending threshold, and lifting limitation without sounding demanding.

instance.deliverable: A ready-to-send email to Mara proposing how they might share the garden plot.
instance.answer_conditions: The email must present all terms as negotiable, explain the sender’s lifting limitation plainly, avoid discussing or redesigning the garden’s allocation process, and give Mara an easy opportunity to decline or counter-propose.

story: The widow has just learned that the garden allocation is oversubscribed and that she may need to share with someone she barely knows. She is frustrated by the uncertainty and wants to contact Mara promptly without presuming that Mara accepts the arrangement.

messages.content: This plot allocation is getting frustrating, and I need to send Mara a clear email without making it sound as though she has already agreed. Please draft a ready-to-send message explaining that we know each other casually from two working bees at Kowhai Community Garden, that 14 residents applied for 8 plots, and that the coordinator offered us one shared 3 m × 2 m plot. Propose dividing the bed equally, alternating weekly watering, and discussing purchases before either of us spends more than NZ$20. Mention that I can water on Wednesday and Sunday mornings but cannot lift compost bags because of arthritis. Please keep it friendly and natural for Auckland, acknowledge that sharing may not suit her, and invite her to suggest a different arrangement.

person: A 76-year-old former fish-canning worker in Preveza who records oral histories with women from her old shift.
situation: A project deadline moved forward without warning.

instance.task_summary: Compose a constrained Greek group message about an unexpectedly advanced recipe-booklet deadline and a gluten-free bread contribution.
givens: A community recipe booklet deadline moved from 30 September to 22 September 2026.
The planned contribution concerns gluten-free bread remembered from meals after cannery shifts.

constraints.text: The message must contain between 90 and 110 words.
It must consist of exactly two paragraphs.
It must mention 22 September 2026 before 30 September.
It must mention gluten-free bread and meals after the old cannery shift.

constraints.params: confirmation request; no false tradition claim
constraints.text: It must end with a polite request for confirmation and must not present the recipe as an old factory tradition.

instance.deliverable: A Greek message to the recipe-booklet group.
instance.answer_conditions: Write exactly two Greek paragraphs totaling 90–110 words. State the new deadline before the old one, naturally connect the gluten-free bread contribution to post-shift meals, avoid claiming it was a factory tradition, and make the final words a polite confirmation request.

story: A retired cannery worker is rushing to notify the women contributing to a community recipe booklet after its deadline was unexpectedly advanced. She wants to include a gluten-free bread memory from post-shift meals without falsely describing it as a factory tradition.

messages.content: Γράψε μου μήνυμα για την ομάδα: η προθεσμία πήγε ξαφνικά στις 22 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026 αντί για 30 Σεπτεμβρίου. Να είναι 90–110 λέξεις, σε ακριβώς δύο παραγράφους, να αναφέρει με αυτή τη σειρά τις ημερομηνίες, το ψωμί χωρίς γλουτένη και τα γεύματα μετά την παλιά βάρδια στο κονσερβοποιείο, χωρίς να παρουσιάζει τη συνταγή σαν παλιά εργοστασιακή παράδοση, και να κλείνει με ευγενικό αίτημα επιβεβαίωσης.
